chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Mismā' al-Basri, who said:

I prayed with Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, and he recited: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful, al-Hamdu lillahi Rabb al-'Alamin. Then he recited the surah after al-Hamd and did not recite Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Then he stood in the second rak'ah and recited al-Hamd and did not recite Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Then he recited another surah.

So this report does not contradict the reports that we have presented earlier, because it contains the account of an action. It is possible that Mismā' did not hear Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام reciting Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim due to a distance between him and the Imam, and it is also possible that he only omitted it due to a kind of taqiyyah and necessity.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, referred to by his kunyah
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment due to circumstances
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: Surat al-Fatihah, referred to here by its opening phrase
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: this report or narration under discussion
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the opening formula recited in the prayer before a surah
key_terms.حِكَايَةَ فِعْلٍ: a report describing an observed act rather than an explicit verbal ruling

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile narrations about not hearing بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ in salat?
ai.summary: This report describes the observed recitation of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام in salat, specifically regarding the recitation of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim before the second surah. The compiler explains that this narration does not conflict with other reports, since the omission may have been due to the listener not hearing it or due to taqiyyah and necessity.
